_meta.source: Reverse-engineered: USB MIDI capture capture of Axe-Edit III traffic + accessibility-driven parameter sweeps. ids are firmware-internal enums.
_meta.warning: Param ids, model ids, and scales are specific to FW 32.02; a firmware update could renumber them. Re-capture to verify on other firmware.

protocol.set_param: F0 00 01 74 10 01 09 00 <blk_lo blk_hi> <pid_lo pid_hi> <v0 v1 v2 v3 v4> 00 00 00 00 <cks> F7
protocol.ids: Block id and param id are 14-bit: lo | (hi<<7)
protocol.value_encoding: Value = displayed_value / scale, encoded as IEEE-754 float32 little-endian, packed as 5 x 7-bit MIDI septets (LSB first)
protocol.checksum: XOR of all bytes from F0 through the last data byte, & 0x7F

scales.null: Nonlinear display (e.g. capacitance) -> store/send the raw float directly

protocol.transport: Send to 'Axe-Fx III MIDI Out'. Works with Axe-Edit open. In mido, sysex data = frame without F0/F7.
protocol.example: Set AMP1 Gain to 7.5: param_id=1, scale=10 -> float 0.75
protocol.alt_set_param_0152: RESOLVED: func 0x01 sub 0x52 is a FIXED alt-SET opcode (NOT block-encoded). Frame layout identical to 01 09 with the sub byte = 0x52. DEVICE-VERIFIED on 3 independent blocks: Flanger Bass Focus (block 0x52, pid 26), Delay Drive (block 0x46, pid 16, scale 10), Cab Drive (block 0x3E, pid 33, scale 10) -- the latter two have block ids != 0x52, which disambiguates (the Flanger 0x52==0x52 was a coincidence). For all of these, plain 01 09 to the SAME numeric pid does NOT set the param (it is unreachable via 01 09 -- a different param namespace). The firmware-added 'Drive' param is an alt-SET class: Delay & Cab Drive verified; Chorus(0x4E pid20), Flanger(0x52 pid20), Rotary(0x56 pid17), Wah(0x5E pid10), DynaDist(0xCA pid7) are pattern-inferred alt-SET (unverified). BUILDER CAVEAT: a SET command emit 01 09 and will silently no-op for these params -- honor the param's set_command='01 52'. Method to find more: direct_probe_map a block, the sliders that 01 09 cannot move are alt-SET candidates; confirm by capturing Axe-Edit's TX. UPDATE: the alt-SET class is BROADER than 'Drive' -- IR Player (0xC3) Low Cut (pid 2) and High Cut (pid 3) are also alt-SET (01 09 no-op, 01 52 works). So 0x52 = the SET command for a set of firmware-added params of any kind, not just Drive.

SCENEMIDI.note: 01 19 GET is DEAD on this block (always 0.0, even for set params) -- display/UIA is the only read oracle.: the 'CC number / CC value / PC number fields are NOT UIA-visible, USB MIDI capture queued' verdict is OVERTURNED -- the Number/Value fields ARE UIA EditControls that only EXIST when the slot's Type is set to CC/PC (never set a slot to CC), and the panel LIVE-repaints on device-direct SETs. Grids cracked by SET-and-watch, no capture needed: Number (CC#) = pids 128-191, Value (CC value / PC#) = pids 192-255, both 128+(scene-1)*8+(slot-1) / 192+(scene-1)*8+(slot-1). Grid-cell display name is 'MIDI Block' (NOT 'Scene MIDI 1'). Panel header shows a 'One Scene' view mode; the grid displays the ACTIVE scene's rows (scene switch via 0x0C repaints). Block cannot be bypassed; sends only on the MIDI OUT DIN.

params.name: Slot 1 Type
params.note: Device-verified enum (SET 1 -> display CC, SET 2 -> display PC, >=2 clamps to PC, 0 -> '--'; both 01 09 and 01 52 store identically). Pids 0-7 are the SCENE 1 bank of an 8x8 per-scene grid -- Type pid = (scene-1)*8 + (slot-1), pids 0-63 (device-verified: values written at pids 8/9/10 appeared as slot 1/2/3 types when the device switched to scene 2).

params.name: Slot 1 Channel
params.note: Per-slot MIDI channel, SHARED across scenes (verified unchanged on scene switch); display = stored+1 (1-16), encoded here as the 16-name enum '1'..'16' -> 0..15 (device-verified: SET 64=5 -> display 6, SET 64=500 clamps -> display 16, SET 65=9 -> slot 2 display 10). NOT linaffine: the codec's linaffine clamps stored to [0,1], which would cap the channel at 2 -- the enum is the lossless combo-native encoding of the same +1 rule.

IRPLAYER.note: Block id 0xC3 (195), verified (Axe-Edit Insert frame 01 32 00 43 01). Params mapped via 01 09 direct-MIDI probe + positional UIA readback. Two IR slots (CAB 1 / CAB 2): per-slot Bank, IR Number (1-based index), IR Length. Shared: Filter Slope, Input Select, Level, Balance, Pan, Mix, Mode (Series/Parallel), Bypass Mode. **Low Cut (pid 2) and High Cut (pid 3) are ALT-SET 0x52 params** (01 09 is a no-op) with a nonlinear log-freq encoding -- this proves the 0x52 alt-SET class is NOT limited to 'Drive'. IR Player 2 = 0xC4 (196) inferred. Empty IR Players are invisible to the 0x13 status dump.

CONTROL.note: Block id 2 (ID_CONTROL) = the CONTROLLERS system block (not a grid effect block: not placeable or bypassable, no instances). Holds LFO 1/2, ADSR 1/2, Envelope, Sequencer (+32 stages), Manual 1-5, Scene Ctrl 1-4, and Pitch Input Source. DEVICE-PERSISTENT: CONTROL writes persist across preset changes and Axe-Edit close -- treat exactly like the GLOBAL block (autosave-like, no reload-to-revert; read/record before any write). Announce laws: combos/enums announce via an unsolicited 01 09 (value = index/(N-1)); continuous sliders do not emit 01 09 -- they announce via the 01 0C/01 0D family (and 01 0A/01 0B for some, e.g. Quantize/Stages), same field layout as 09. Modifiers: 01 07 is NOT the modifier-slot read (it reads all-zero even with a modifier attached); the real modifier-slot read is fn 0x1F on slot blocks 3-26, and attach/detach use 01 3a / 01 3b -- see ADVANCED_COMMANDS.md. READ-ONLY: pids 171-174 are write-deaf display-mark (X/Y) coordinates. DO-NOT-WRITE hot zone: pids 178-188 are set-all action pids -- never probe-write above pid 174. Tempo: preset tempo = pid 32 (SET = 01 09 raw BPM float), Tempo To Use = pid 33 {Preset, Global}; func 0x14 is GET-only and returns the stale stored preset tempo; the live global tempo is GLOBAL block pid 0.

params.name: Tempo
params.note: Device: the preset/current tempo. SET works via plain 01 09 with the RAW BPM float (SET 97.0 -> UI '97 BPM' instantly; the Axe-Fx II precedent pid 32 holds EXACTLY on the III). UI slider 250->120 moved exactly this one block-2 pid. GET taper is approximate/change-detect ONLY: ~linear but NOT (BPM-30)/220 -- observed 250->1.0000, 120->0.4248, 97->0.3230; best 2-point linear fit ~ (BPM-24)/226. SET is exact, GET approximate. Func 0x14 does NOT set tempo, and (correction) does NOT read the global tempo either -- it returns the STORED (flash) preset tempo (stale). The GLOBAL tempo lives at GLOBAL (id 1) pid 0 (SET = raw BPM).

GLOBAL.note: Block id 1 = the GLOBAL SETTINGS block (a SYSTEM block, not a grid effect block: not placeable or bypassable, no instances). AUTOSAVE WARNING: these are persistent device settings, not edit-buffer state -- writes take effect immediately and are autosaved, with no reload-to-revert. The only way to undo a write is to write the old value back, so read and record the current value before changing anything. The block uses the full 14-bit parameter-id space (settings continue well above the visible range); a passive GET (01 19) answers on every pid. The device announces every settings change as an unsolicited 01 09 frame on block 1 (value normalized; enums broadcast as index/(N-1)), so a passive listen plus one front-panel change captures a pid for free. SET semantics: continuous sliders take a plain 01 09 with the raw display value; combos/enums take 01 09 with float(enum index). DO-NOT-SET text regions: pids 8470-12949 (Song names @8470 stride 5, section names @9110) and 14617+ (Setlist names) are 16-bit character-pair text storage -- writing parameter floats there corrupts Songs/Setlists text; never SET them. Notable params: Global Tempo pid 0; Input 1 Gain pid 8367 (log taper, SET by raw display value); External Control 1-8 input-source selectors pids 80-87; six bipolar +/-25 offset knobs pids 9-14; Metronome levels pids 119-121.
